# Lab 13 — Threads that share nothing, and one counter that is shared

**Unit:** [week 13, concurrency](../../week13-concurrency-project.md)
(exercises 1–2). **Time:** 2 hours. **Runs in the playground:** no

The playground runs one WebAssembly program without threads, and its
older compiler rejects the solution with a type error. Run this lab with
`fid`.

Spawned functions get copies of their arguments, so most concurrent code
shares nothing. A global is shared, and the compiler rejects an unlocked
write to it from a spawned function. You add the lock, then restructure a
fork-join count with `parallel`.

## Start

- [Open the starter in the playground](https://fides-lang.org/playground#) to read it, and
- copy [`starter.fd`](starter.fd) and run `fid check starter.fd`. It is
  rejected.

## Tasks

1. **Read the error.** Which function, which global, which rule
   (reference §10)? With `use sync;`, create one mutex in `main`
   (`sync_mutex_create`) in a global, and hold it
   (`sync_mutex_lock`/`sync_mutex_unlock`) around the write of `served`.
2. **Count.** After both requests are joined, print `served <n>`.
3. **Fork-join.** Replace the two `spawn`/`await` pairs of the word count
   by one `parallel { | a = count_long(left, 7); | b = count_long(right, 7); }`
   statement (reference §10.3).

## Check your work

When you are done, `fid run starter.fd` prints:

```text
responses 30
served 2
long words: 7 of 8
```

## Questions to hand in

- The race check accepts `handle` once it calls a function named like a
  lock. Write a version that it accepts and that is still racy (week 13,
  §3), and explain why the checker cannot see it.
- Explain, using only rules from this course, why the two counting
  threads can never free the same `str`.
